title: Forge
description: A terminal workspace for coordinating coding agents in separate Git worktrees, with persistent sessions and a CLI.
role: Independent project: workflow design, AI-assisted implementation and review. TODO-VERIFY: confirm ownership wording and current release status.
problem: Parallel coding agents need isolated checkouts, controllable terminal sessions and a way to inspect work before integration. A window closing should not be the same thing as a terminal task ending.

decisions.title: Isolate each agent's working tree
decisions.decision: In worktree-isolation mode, agents can use separate branches and Git worktrees.
decisions.tradeoff: TODO-VERIFY: confirm the mode's behavior and design rationale. Isolation avoids competing edits in one checkout, but integration and worktree cleanup still need review.

decisions.title: Separate engine and window lifetimes
decisions.decision: A background engine hosts real terminal sessions using node-pty and headless xterm; the UI attaches to that engine.
decisions.tradeoff: TODO-VERIFY: confirm recovery guarantees. A persistent engine introduces ownership, reconnection and orphan-process concerns.

decisions.title: Require explicit execution
decisions.decision: Agents start or resume explicitly. Local IPC uses an owner card and token; the CLI exposes start, send, read, wait and stop operations.
decisions.tradeoff: TODO-VERIFY: verify the precise threat model. Explicit control adds user steps, while local credentials require lifecycle management.

decisions.title: Make review a separate workflow
decisions.decision: The documented review flow separates checks, auditors and a verifier. Lead MCP relies on host-provided security.
decisions.tradeoff: TODO-VERIFY: explain the implemented handoff and its limits. More reviewers add time and do not guarantee correctness.

results.value: Open-source workspace and CLI for real coding-agent terminals; the README describes Windows and Linux build checks.
